anchor: She was a phantom of delight
note: Phantom: a ghost, or an image seen but not touched. Here, a vision of the woman as she first appeared.

anchor: A lovely apparition
note: Apparition: a sudden, ghostlike appearance.

anchor: To haunt, to startle, and waylay
note: Waylay: to wait in hiding and stop someone on the way.

anchor: For transient sorrows, simple wiles
note: Transient: lasting only a short time. Wiles: small tricks and charms.

anchor: The very pulse of the machine
note: Machine: here, the human body, which works like a machine.

anchor: A maid whom there were none to praise
note: Maid: a young unmarried woman, a girl.

anchor: an overseeing power
note: Overseeing: watching over and guiding.

anchor: Of mute insensate things
note: Insensate: without feeling or awareness.

anchor: Where rivulets dance their wayward round
note: Rivulets: small streams. Wayward: turning where they please.

anchor: Here in this happy dell
note: Dell: a small, wooded valley.

anchor: Roll’d round in earth’s diurnal course
note: Diurnal: happening every day, such as the earth’s daily turning.

anchor: The mind’s least generous wish a mendicant
note: Mendicant: a beggar, someone who lives by asking for gifts.

anchor: Than a forsaken bird’s-nest fill’d with snow
note: Forsaken: abandoned, left by everyone.

anchor: ’Mid its own bush of leafless eglantine
note: Eglantine: sweetbrier, a wild rose with thorny stems.

anchor: Surprized by joy—impatient as the wind
note: Surprized: an old spelling of “surprised.”

anchor: I turn’d to share the transport
note: Transport: a strong feeling of joy that carries one away.

anchor: That spot which no vicissitude can find
note: Vicissitude: a change in fortune, a turn of luck, good or bad.

anchor: Stern Daughter of the voice of God!
note: Daughter of the voice of God: Duty is pictured as the child of God’s command.

anchor: a rod To check the erring, and reprove
note: Reprove: to scold gently, to correct.

anchor: When empty terrors overawe
note: Overawe: to hold in fear and wonder.

anchor: Upon the genial sense of youth
note: Genial: cheerful and warm, friendly.

anchor: When love is an unerring light
note: Unerring: never making a mistake.

anchor: Thy timely mandate, I deferr’d
note: Mandate: an order or command. Deferr’d: put off till later.

anchor: Or strong compunction in me wrought
note: Compunction: a pang of conscience, sorrow at having done wrong.

anchor: I supplicate for thy controul
note: Supplicate: to ask humbly, to beg.

anchor: Me this uncharter’d freedom tires
note: Uncharter’d: not bound by any rule or law, wholly free.

anchor: thy bondman let me live
note: Bondman: a servant or slave bound to a master.

anchor: Thou from thy Alpine holds at length are driven
note: In 1802 the French under Napoleon had overrun Switzerland (1800), driving liberty from its mountain strongholds.
source: F. T. Palgrave, The Golden Treasury (1861), Palgrave’s Notes, Poem 210, https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/19221

anchor: Once did She hold the gorgeous East in fee
note: In fee: in full possession, as a feudal lord holds land.

anchor: the eldest child of liberty
note: Venice lost its independence in 1797, when the last doge gave up his office and the city passed under Napoleon.
source: Encyclopædia Britannica, 11th ed. (1911), “Doge”, https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/1911_Encyclop%C3%A6dia_Britannica/Doge; F. T. Palgrave, The Golden Treasury (1861), Palgrave’s Notes, Poem 211, https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/19221

anchor: She must espouse the everlasting Sea
note: Each year the doge of Venice cast a ring into the Adriatic in a symbolic marriage of the city to the sea.

anchor: our life is only drest
note: Drest: dressed, here meaning put on for show.

anchor: Rapine, avarice, expense
note: Rapine: seizing goods by force, plunder. Avarice: greed for money.

anchor: This is idolatry
note: Idolatry: worship of idols, or devotion to something that is not God.

anchor: Plain living and high thinking are no more
note: A famous line: simple habits of life joined to noble thoughts, which Wordsworth thought had vanished.

anchor: Milton! thou shouldst be living at this hour
note: John Milton was the great English poet of Paradise Lost, who also wrote for the Puritan cause in the Civil War. Wordsworth calls on him to rouse England.

anchor: she is a fen Of stagnant waters
note: Fen: low, marshy land. Stagnant: still and foul, not flowing.

anchor: Have forfeited their ancient English dower
note: Forfeited: lost by wrongdoing. Dower: a gift or inheritance.

anchor: When men change swords for ledgers
note: Ledgers: account books in which business records are kept.

anchor: Of those unfilial fears I am ashamed
note: Unfilial: not fitting for a loving child, here toward one’s country.

anchor: In thee a bulwark of the cause of men
note: Bulwark: a strong wall or defense.

anchor: In the sweet shire of Cardigan
note: Cardigan, or Cardiganshire, is a hilly county of west Wales, by Cardigan Bay on the Irish Sea.

anchor: A running huntsman merry
note: Huntsman: a man who leads the hounds in a hunt.

anchor: When Echo bandied round and round
note: Bandied: tossed back and forth, as in a game.

anchor: The halloo of Simon Lee
note: Halloo: a loud shout used to call hounds or attract attention.

anchor: For husbandry or tillage
note: Husbandry: farming. Tillage: plowing and working the soil.

anchor: In liveried poverty
note: Liveried: dressed in a servant’s uniform, called livery.

anchor: His body dwindled and awry
note: Awry: twisted to one side, crooked.

anchor: Rests upon ankles swoln and thick
note: Swoln: an old form of “swollen,” puffed up and thick.

anchor: The mattock totter’d in his hand
note: Mattock: a digging tool like a pickaxe, with a flat blade.

anchor: Give me your tool,“ to him I said
note: Tool: a hand implement for work, here Simon’s mattock.

anchor: my proffer’d aid
note: Proffer’d: offered, held out for someone to take.

anchor: The tangled root I sever’d
note: Sever’d: cut apart, cut clean through.

anchor: There is a flower, the Lesser Celandine
note: Lesser celandine: a small yellow wild flower that blooms in early spring.

anchor: And buffeted at will by rain and storm
note: Buffeted: struck again and again, battered.

anchor: with inly-mutter’d voice
note: Inly: inwardly, in the heart or mind.

anchor: And, in my spleen, I smiled that it was gray
note: Spleen: a fit of bad temper or low spirits.

anchor: To be a prodigal’s favourite
note: Prodigal: one who wastes money recklessly.

anchor: A miser’s pensioner
note: Miser: a stingy person who hoards money. Pensioner: one who lives on a small allowance.

anchor: No tidings of an only child
note: Tidings: news, word about what has happened.

anchor: Ingenuous, innocent, and bold
note: Ingenuous: simple, open, and innocent.

anchor: Maim’d, mangled by inhuman men
note: Maim’d: crippled by a wound. Mangled: badly torn up.

anchor: An incommunicable sleep
note: Incommunicable: that cannot be shared or told to others.

anchor: That there was ever intercourse
note: Intercourse: contact and communication between people.

anchor: My apprehensions come in crowds
note: Apprehensions: anxious fears about what may happen.

anchor: Beyond participation lie
note: Participation: sharing in something with others.

anchor: Ethereal Minstrel! pilgrim of the sky!
note: Ethereal: light and airy, seeming to belong to heaven. Minstrel: a singer.

anchor: Or while the wings aspire
note: Aspire: to rise high, to long for something lofty.

anchor: Mount, daring warbler!
note: Warbler: a bird that sings in trills.

anchor: True to the kindred points of Heaven and Home!
note: Kindred: related, of the same kind.

anchor: In this sequester’d nook how sweet
note: Sequester’d: secluded, tucked away. Nook: a small, quiet corner.

anchor: In all this covert of the blest
note: Covert: a thicket where birds and animals hide.

anchor: In joy of voice and pinion
note: Pinion: a bird’s wing, or its outer feathers.

anchor: Make all one band of paramours
note: Paramours: lovers, those who are in love with each other.

anchor: Behold him perch’d in ecstasies
note: Ecstasies: states of overwhelming joy.

anchor: The voiceless Form he chose to feign
note: Feign: to pretend, to put on a false appearance.

anchor: O blithe new-comer!
note: Blithe: cheerful and carefree, light of heart.

anchor: Of visionary hours
note: Visionary: seen in imagination, dreamlike.

anchor: till I do beget
note: Beget: to bring into being.

anchor: An unsubstantial, fairy place
note: Unsubstantial: not solid or real, like a dream.

anchor: In his first splendour valley, rock, or hill
note: Splendour: great brightness and beauty.

anchor: Whom mere despite of heart could so far please
note: Despite: spite, ill will, a mean desire to hurt.

anchor: And love of havoc
note: Havoc: widespread destruction and ruin.

anchor: Fame taxes him
note: Taxes: here, accuses or blames him for.

anchor: a noble horde
note: Horde: a large crowd, here the trees that stood together.

anchor: Many hearts deplored
note: Deplored: felt or expressed deep sorrow for.

anchor: the gentle Tweed
note: The Tweed is a river of southern Scotland that flows east to the North Sea.

anchor: But covet not the abode
note: Covet: to long for what belongs to another.

anchor: repining while they look
note: Repining: complaining and unhappy over what one lacks.

anchor: This precious leaf with harsh impiety
note: Impiety: lack of reverence, disrespect for what is holy.

anchor: The roses to the porch which they entwine
note: Entwine: to twist around, to wind together.

anchor: is thy earthly dower
note: Dower: a natural gift or endowment.

anchor: have shed Their utmost bounty on thy head
note: Bounty: generosity, a gift freely given.

anchor: never saw I mien or face
note: Mien: a person’s look or manner.

anchor: Benignity and home-bred sense
note: Benignity: kindness and gentleness of nature.

anchor: shamefacedness
note: Shamefacedness: shyness and modesty, a blush of bashfulness.

anchor: And seemliness complete
note: Seemliness: proper, becoming conduct that suits the occasion.

anchor: A bondage sweetly brook’d
note: Brook’d: put up with, endured.

anchor: a garland cull
note: Garland: a wreath of flowers. Cull: to pick out and gather.

anchor: Among the farthest Hebrides
note: The Hebrides are a group of islands off the west coast of Scotland, also called the Western Isles.

anchor: Perhaps the plaintive numbers flow
note: Plaintive: sad and mournful. Numbers: verses, lines of song.

anchor: o’er the sickle bending
note: Sickle: a curved hand blade for cutting grain.

anchor: In such a jocund company
note: Jocund: cheerful, merry, full of high spirits.

anchor: Oft on the dappled turf at ease
note: Dappled: marked with spots or patches of light and shade.

anchor: I sit and play with similes
note: Similes: comparisons using “like” or “as.” The poet likens the daisy to many things.

anchor: A nun demure, of lowly port
note: Demure: quiet and modest. Port: bearing, the way one carries oneself.

anchor: A starveling in a scanty vest
note: Starveling: a person or animal thin with hunger.

anchor: Thy appellations
note: Appellations: names, titles given to something.

anchor: A little Cyclops, with one eye
note: In Greek myth the Cyclopes were giants with one round eye in the middle of the forehead.

anchor: I call thee and to that cleave fast
note: Cleave: to hold fast, to cling.

anchor: Do thou, as thou art wont, repair
note: Wont: accustomed. Repair: to mend, to restore.

anchor: From Stirling castle we had seen
note: Stirling is a Scottish town on the River Forth, once guarded by a royal castle on a high rock.

anchor: The mazy Forth unravell’d
note: The Forth is a river of eastern Scotland that winds in great loops. Mazy: winding like a maze.

anchor: banks of Clyde and Tay
note: The Clyde flows through western Scotland, and the Tay is the longest river in Scotland.
source: Encyclopædia Britannica, 11th ed. (1911), “Clyde”, https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/1911_Encyclop%C3%A6dia_Britannica/Clyde; Encyclopædia Britannica, 11th ed. (1911), “Tay”, https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/1911_Encyclop%C3%A6dia_Britannica/Tay

anchor: And with the Tweed had travell’d
note: The Tweed is a river of southern Scotland that flows east to the North Sea.

anchor: my “winsome Marrow.”
note: Winsome: pleasing and charming. Marrow: in Scots, a mate or companion.

anchor: Whate’er betide, we’ll turn aside
note: Betide: to happen, to come to pass.

anchor: the Braes of Yarrow
note: The Yarrow is a river and valley in Selkirkshire, in the south of Scotland. Braes: hillsides.

anchor: frae Selkirk town
note: Selkirk is the county town of Selkirkshire in southern Scotland. Frae means “from” in Scots.

anchor: Galla Water, Leader Haughs
note: Haughs: low meadows beside a river.

anchor: pleasant Tiviotdale
note: Teviotdale is the valley of the River Teviot in the south of Scotland, in Roxburghshire.

anchor: O green,” said I, “are Yarrow’s holms
note: Holms: low river-meadows, flat land beside a stream.

anchor: O’er hilly path, and open strath
note: Strath: a wide river valley.

anchor: or we shall rue it
note: Rue: to regret bitterly, to be sorry for.

anchor: The water-Wraith ascended thrice
note: Wraith: a ghostly image of a living person, often seen as a sign of coming death.

anchor: And on my true-love’s forehead plant A crest of blooming heather
note: Heather: a low wild shrub with small purple flowers, common on Scottish hills.

anchor: And what if I enwreathed my own?
note: Enwreathed: crowned with a wreath.

anchor: Accordant to the measure
note: Accordant: in agreement with, in tune.

anchor: Thou liest in Abraham’s bosom all the year
note: In Jesus’s parable the poor man Lazarus is carried after death to “Abraham’s bosom,” the place of the blessed.
source: The Bible (King James Version), Luke 16:22, https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/10

anchor: The periwinkle trail’d its wreaths
note: Periwinkle: a trailing evergreen plant with blue flowers.

anchor: There came a youth from Georgia’s shore
note: Georgia was a British colony on the southeast coast of North America. The story is set at the time of the American Revolution.

anchor: A military casque he wore
note: Casque: a helmet, a piece of armor for the head.

anchor: He brought them from the Cherokees
note: The Cherokees were a Native American people of the southeastern United States, a land of mountains and forests.

anchor: From battle and from jeopardy
note: Jeopardy: danger, risk of harm or loss.

anchor: Were perilous to hear
note: Perilous: full of danger, very risky.

anchor: He told of girls, a happy rout
note: Rout: a crowd, a noisy company.

anchor: He told of the Magnolia
note: Magnolia: a tree of the southern United States with large, sweet-smelling white flowers.

anchor: The cypress and her spire
note: Cypress: a tall, narrow evergreen tree.

anchor: The youth of green savannahs spake
note: Savannahs: wide, flat, grassy plains with few trees.

anchor: A sylvan huntress
note: Sylvan: of the woods, living in the forest.

anchor: We in the church our faith will plight
note: Plight: to pledge, to promise solemnly.

anchor: This Stripling, sportive, gay, and bold
note: Stripling: a young man, not yet fully grown.

anchor: And such impetuous blood
note: Impetuous: rushing, acting suddenly without thought.

anchor: Nor less, to feed voluptuous thought
note: Voluptuous: given to pleasures of the senses.

anchor: I ween That sometimes
note: Ween: to suppose, to believe.

anchor: She fearfully caroused
note: Caroused: made merry, drank and sang noisily.

anchor: There came a respite to her pain
note: Respite: a short rest, a pause in suffering.

anchor: The vernal leaves
note: Vernal: of spring, belonging to the spring season.

anchor: Nor ever tax’d them with the ill
note: Tax’d: accused, blamed for a fault.

anchor: This flute, made of a hemlock stalk
note: Hemlock: a tall plant with hollow stems and poisonous juice.

anchor: in hallow’d mould
note: Hallow’d: made holy, blessed. Mould: loose earth, the grave.

anchor: Elysian quiet, without toil or strife
note: Elysium, or the Elysian Fields, was the Greek paradise where the blessed lived in peace after death.

anchor: A deep distress hath humanised my soul
note: Humanised: made gentler and more feeling. The distress was the death of Wordsworth’s brother John at sea.
source: F. T. Palgrave, The Golden Treasury (1861), Palgrave’s Notes, Poem 276, https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/19221

anchor: Then, Beaumont, Friend!
note: Sir George Beaumont painted the picture of Peele Castle in a storm. Wordsworth wrote the poem after his brother John was lost in a shipwreck.
source: F. T. Palgrave, The Golden Treasury (1861), Palgrave’s Notes, Poem 276, https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/19221

anchor: This rueful sky, this pageantry of fear!
note: Rueful: causing sorrow or pity. Pageantry: a grand, showy display.

anchor: a sordid boon!
note: Sordid: dirty, low, and mean. Boon: a gift or favor.

anchor: A Pagan suckled in a creed outworn
note: Pagan: a worshipper of old gods, such as the Greek gods. Creed: a belief held by a religion.

anchor: standing on this pleasant lea
note: Lea: open grassland, a meadow.

anchor: Have sight of Proteus rising from the sea
note: In Greek myth Proteus was a sea god who kept changing shape. He stands for the sea’s constant change and sameness.
source: F. T. Palgrave, The Golden Treasury (1861), Palgrave’s Notes, Poem 278, https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/19221

anchor: Tax not the royal Saint with vain expense
note: The royal Saint is Henry VI, founder of King’s College, Cambridge. Wordsworth defends the great sums spent on its chapel.
source: F. T. Palgrave, The Golden Treasury (1861), Palgrave’s Notes, Poem 279, https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/19221

anchor: Albeit labouring for a scanty band
note: Albeit: although, even though, in spite of the fact that.

anchor: the lore Of nicely-calculated less or more
note: Lore: knowledge, learning. Nicely: here, with fine exactness.

anchor: With rod and line I sued the sport
note: Sued: pursued, went after. The old man had been fishing.

anchor: Beside the church-yard yew
note: Yew: a dark evergreen tree often planted in churchyards.

anchor: Of wilding in his hand
note: Wilding: a wild apple tree, or its fruit.

anchor: or catch
note: Catch: a round, a short song in which singers take up the tune in turn.

anchor: Let loose their carols
note: Carols: joyful songs, here the songs of birds.

anchor: And, ere we came to Leonard’s Rock
note: Ere: before (an old-fashioned word).

anchor: The Child is father of the Man
note: A famous line: the child’s feelings and habits shape the adult he will become.

anchor: Bound each to each by natural piety
note: Piety: reverence and devotion, here a natural respect for life.

anchor: Apparell’d in celestial light
note: Apparell’d: clothed, dressed. Celestial: heavenly.

anchor: as it hath been of yore
note: Of yore: in times long past.

anchor: And while the young lambs bound As to the tabor’s sound
note: Tabor: a small drum used to accompany a pipe.

anchor: The cataracts blow their trumpets from the steep
note: Cataracts: waterfalls, here roaring down the mountain.

anchor: My head hath its coronal
note: Coronal: a crown or wreath for the head.

anchor: Whither is fled the visionary gleam?
note: Visionary gleam: the dreamlike brightness that childhood once cast over the world.

anchor: A six years’ darling of a pigmy size
note: Pigmy: tiny, a very small person.

anchor: Fretted by sallies of his mother’s kisses
note: Sallies: sudden bursts. Fretted: here, teased and troubled.

anchor: The little actor cons another part
note: Cons: studies carefully, learns by heart.

anchor: That life brings with her in her equipage
note: Equipage: the carriage, servants, and gear that go with a person.

anchor: Thou, whose exterior semblance doth belie
note: Belie: to give a false picture of. Semblance: outward appearance.

anchor: Full soon thy soul shall have her earthly freight
note: Freight: a load carried, here the burden of earthly cares.

anchor: What was so fugitive
note: Fugitive: fleeting, quickly passing away.

anchor: Perpetual benediction
note: Benediction: a blessing, an expression of thanks.

anchor: But for those obstinate questionings
note: Obstinate: stubborn, refusing to give up.

anchor: Blank misgivings of a creature
note: Misgivings: feelings of doubt or fear.

anchor: In the primal sympathy
note: Primal: first, original, belonging to the beginning.

anchor: Forebode not any severing of our loves!
note: Forebode: to warn of a coming evil. Severing: cutting apart.

anchor: I only have relinquish’d one delight
note: Relinquish’d: given up, let go of willingly.

anchor: man’s mortality
note: Mortality: the fact that every person must die.

anchor: Another race hath been, and other palms are won
note: Palms: here, the prizes of victory, as in a race.
